COUNTERMEASURE-20260603-GATE3-STAGE07-TRANSPORT-RESUME detail:

- Symptom: the v7 model-transport/rate-limit Andon showed that a required Stage
  07 expansion subprocess failed before final assembly, and the runner had no
  bounded retry/resume policy for that exact subprocess.
- Failed check: failed subprocess
  `stage-07-release-output restorative-response expansion 1`; read-only v7
  preflight classified its log as retryable transport with websocket
  `403 Forbidden` retries, HTTP fallback, and `429 Too Many Requests`.
- Owner file / owner surface: `tools/run_staged_current_skill_smoke.py` Stage
  07 expansion subprocess loop and v7 ignored run artifacts under
  `.daee/staged-row-family-smokes/20260602-secularism-pilot-v7/`.
- 5 Whys: v7 failed because the expansion subprocess could not obtain a model
  response; the failed call stopped the pilot because the runner treated a
  single transport failure as terminal; that happened because there was no
  retryable-transport classifier, attempt metadata, or hash-bound resume
  preflight; prior repairs targeted semantic assembly contracts and heading
  canonicalization, not transport lifecycle; recurrence is prevented by
  runner-owned bounded retries, exact failed-subprocess resume, hash-match
  gates, no-output/no-sidecar refusal gates, and no-model canaries.
- Hansei: transport failure and semantic output failure need different custody
  records. A rate-limited expansion must not consume proof-surface semantics or
  invite unbounded reruns.
- Countermeasure: add retryable transport classification,
  `--transport-retry-rounds`, `--resume-run-dir`, per-subprocess attempt
  metadata, v7 resume preflight using the prior hash record and failure record,
  manifest `transport_resume` lineage, and no-model self-test canaries for
  retry classification, semantic non-retryability, hash mismatch, existing
  final output, existing sidecars, failed/success attempts, and retry-budget
  exhaustion.
- Smoke B command/result: PASS: `python tools\run_staged_current_skill_smoke.py --self-test`;
  read-only v7 preflight helper returned `section_id=restorative-response`,
  `round=1`, `websocket_403_count=8`, HTTP fallback true, HTTP 429 true, and
  retryable true; focused Smoke B passed; full Windows-correct local
  CI-equivalent checker suite passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Remaining blocker or closure: source repair closed at non-release
  source/docs/checker commit `7782a10963d25499fd1eef846347d06dc9e288d8`,
  GitHub CI `26866227574` PASS, and Pages `26866226870` PASS. The exactly-one
  bounded v7 resume may open only after this post-push status refresh is also
  committed/pushed.

## Corrected Goal Scope - 2026-05-24

The active IMPLEMENTAUDIT goal is expanded beyond the prior manual-smoke release gate. The original
manual-smoke regression objective remains required, but it is now a subgoal of the full
`VISION.md` implementation target. Do not silently downgrade the rows below into future-only notes.

The goal is not met by design notes, VISION prose, a passing one-case smoke, or static fixtures alone.
Each required layer needs source-owned implementation, checker or fixture coverage, fresh behavior
proof where behavior is involved, negative canaries for false passes, and an orchestrator row marked
DONE with evidence. Release remains blocked until every behavior row is DONE and provenance is clean.

## Formalism Execution Requirements - 2026-05-24

The corrected goal requires a formalism-execution audit, not merely ACT syntax, smoke matrix, or
public render compliance. TTP activation and MRP emergence must be produced by daee formalism
itself and be auditable as state-transition grammar.

TTP execution proof requires:

```text
matched pressure
-> selected source-owned owner/TTP
-> owner operation
-> target pressure
-> mechanism/action
-> local state change Delta kappa / Delta nB
-> contribution-to-Land
-> Land(nB)
-> R(H,Delta)
```

MRP formal emergence proof requires:

```text
Land(nB)
-> Delta nB / Delta kappa
-> R(H,Delta)
-> route-gradient / ∇
-> ∇·T / ∇×T where licensed
-> MRP pressure read
-> resultant: held_burden_activation | generated_burden_instantiation |
   no_new_resultant | hold_partial | loopbreak | STOP
-> source-owned owner/TTP route
-> Layer B execution
-> Land
-> R(H,Delta) again
```

The checker and witness layers must not pass an output merely because it contains `[Mid-Reread
Pressure]`, `MRP(nB)`, a graph edge, a generated burden label, or a plausible resultant word. They
must prove the MRP section is downstream of Land, tied to Delta/R(H,Delta), has held/generated
provenance, re-enters owner routing, executes a Layer B owner body, and is mirrored in witness
surfaces.

Formalism-to-witness agreement is required for every burden cycle across:

- Layer B body
- ACT record
- MRP resultant
- Land line
- R(H,Delta)
- Closure/Reconstruction Witness
- `field_witness`
- Output Grapher graph_delta

If any surface claims a transition and another omits or contradicts it, the proof fails or becomes
HOLD/PARTIAL. If ∇, ∇·T, or ∇×T are only notation today, classify them as `OPEN FORMALISM TARGET -
not implemented proof` until source paths, checker rules, fixtures, and fresh outputs prove
otherwise.

Formalism audit lane:

- Name: `daee-formalism-emergence-auditor`
- Scope: audit whether TTP activation, MRP emergence, R(H,Delta), ∇, ∇·T, and ∇×T are executable
  state-transition grammar rather than rhetorical notation.
- Authority: read-only unless reassigned to a narrow patch surface; no release/package/tag/upload
  authority.
- Required report: `Formalism Emergence Audit` with verdict, TTP proof, MRP emergence proof,
  R(H,Delta), ∇, ∇·T, ∇×T, witness/Grapher agreement, decorative notation found, required patches,
  fixtures/canaries, and open rows.

## Architecture Finding: Per-Activation Proof Enables, But Does Not Equal, Graph-Level Collapse Proof

Status: `OPEN / TARGET GUARANTEE`

Dependency: `ACT Canonicalization / Compliance Stabilizer`

Classification:

- Useful architectural finding; not behavior proof.
- Not release readiness.
- Do not claim total collapse, graph completeness, NLA reconstructibility, progressive disclosure completeness, or field-wide reproducibility from per-activation canonicalization alone.

Layer distinction:

- Layer 1, per-activation verification: owner/TTP route selected; `body_ref` dereferences; body performs owner operation; pressure is targeted; `Δκ` / `ΔⁿB` is visible; Land contribution is licensed; `field_witness` mirrors activation.
- Layer 2, graph-level collapse verification: all diagnosed deformations represented as nodes; every node has verified activation or honest HOLD/PARTIAL; generated `𝔅_MRP` nodes are not backfilled into `𝔅_LA`; Land contributions chain correctly; recursion terminates honestly; no unresolved/orphan deformation remains hidden.

Correct conditional guarantee:

`For any input whose deformations are fully diagnosed by the rubric, and whose deformation nodes are all matched to catalogue-backed owner/TTP operations, the runtime should either produce a checker-verified, field_witness-mirrored, graphable collapse proof, or honestly return HOLD/PARTIAL with unmatched or unresolved nodes named.`

Classification row additions:

| Claim | Safe classification |
|---|---|
| Formal notation compliance | PARTIAL: improved by checker canonicalization; structurally closed only if model no longer authors authoritative notation or renderer derives notation from canonical state |
| Heuristic operator governance | PARTIAL: requires owner catalogue operation validation across fresh matrix |
| Per-activation reproducibility | NEEDS PROOF: requires repeated same-case runs showing stable canonical activations |
| NLA encode direction | FOUNDATION LAID: activation extraction can serve as encoder, but not complete |
| NLA decode direction | OPEN: needs explicit ACT/canonical object to natural-language reconstruction layer |
| Progressive skill disclosure | COMPATIBLE, NOT PROVEN: needs direct-routability proof and owner-load behavior |
| Graph-level collapse proof | OPEN: needs graph completeness checker |
| Total `𝔅` field reproducibility | OPEN: depends on graph layer and repeated-run isomorphism |
| field_witness proof certificate | PARTIAL: currently structural; target is graph-completeness certificate |

New backlog row:

`Graph-Level Collapse / field_witness Completeness`

Status: `OPEN — depends on stable per-activation canonicalization`

Required proof:

```text
diagnosed_set == graph.nodes.deformations
∀ node ∈ diagnosed_set:
    node has verified activation
    OR node has explicit HOLD/PARTIAL with reason

∀ activation:
    body_ref dereferences
    owner/TTP operation verified
    Δ verified
    Land contribution verified
    field_witness mirror exists

∀ generated burden:
    provenance is 𝔅_MRP
    not backfilled into 𝔅_LA

collapse_complete = true only if no unresolved node remains
```

Future checker direction:

- Suggested name: `tools\check_field_witness_graph_completeness.py`
- It should verify diagnosed deformation nodes, `𝔅_LA` / `𝔅_MRP` / `𝔅_total` union semantics, terminal status per burden, verified activation per LANDED node, generated-node provenance, no orphan nodes, honest recursion termination, and Closure Witness / field_witness / Output Grapher agreement.
- SVG / Output Grapher is a human-auditable render of the certificate, not proof by itself.

Overclaim guard:

- Do not say: "notation drift is fully solved", "operator governance is closed", "total noetic field collapse is proven", "field_witness guarantees collapse", "same input produces reproducible graph", "all deformations are diagnosed", or "owner catalogue is complete".
- Safe wording: "per-activation canonicalization is being stabilized"; "operator governance is checkable where owner/operation catalogue data exists"; "graph-level collapse proof is a target checker"; "field_witness can become a proof certificate after graph completeness is implemented"; "reproducibility requires repeated-run isomorphism proof"; "diagnostic completeness is a bounded rubric claim"; "unmatched nodes must produce HOLD/PARTIAL, not hallucinated closure".

Sequencing:

- Do not start graph-level collapse checker until narrow Trinitarian per-activation proof is green, strict ACT/MRP passes, field_witness mirror agreement passes, and at least one repeated-run stability check passes or is classified.

## Architecture Finding: Shannon / Integral Trace / field_witness Convergence

Status: `OPEN — ARCHITECTURAL FORMALIZATION TARGET`

Classification:

- Not implemented.
- Not release readiness.
- Do not claim total collapse, entropy reduction, graph convergence, or reproducibility from this framing.

Core insight:

```text
input noetic field
→ diagnosed burden set: 𝔅 = 𝔅_LA ∪ 𝔅_MRP
→ per-burden owner/TTP activation
→ checker-verified Δκ / ΔⁿB
→ licensed Land contribution
→ field_witness graph certificate
→ restorative public render
```

Safe formal framing:

```text
CollapseProof(Φ) =
  fold over 𝔅_total = 𝔅_LA ∪ 𝔅_MRP
  where each node contributes only if:
    owner/TTP route is catalogue-backed;
    body_ref dereferences;
    operation is performed;
    pressure is targeted;
    Δκ / ΔⁿB is visible;
    Land contribution is licensed;
    field_witness mirrors source/target/activation.
```

Research notation, provisional only:

```text
Collapse(Φ) ≈ Fold_{B ∈ 𝔅_total}(verified τ(B), Δκ(B), Land(B))
```

Do not claim `Collapse(Φ) = ∫_B τ(B) · Δκ(B) dB` until the repo defines `dB`, the measure/ordering of `Δκ`, `H(Φ)`, `H_fiṭrah`, and convergence checking.

|---|---|---|
| Shannon / encoding-decoding formalization | OPEN TARGET | ACT canonicalization |
| Integral trace / finite fold over burden graph | OPEN TARGET | graph completeness checker |
| field_witness convergence certificate | OPEN TARGET | owner_activation mirror + graph completeness |
| graph-level collapse proof | OPEN TARGET | per-activation proof stable |
| repeated-run graph reproducibility | OPEN TARGET | stable graph certificate + repeated smoke runs |
| Boltzmann Brain stress case | FUTURE SMOKE | graph-level checker |

Future checker direction:

- Suggested name: `tools\check_field_witness_convergence.py`
- It should verify diagnosed deformation coverage, `𝔅_LA`, `𝔅_MRP`, generated provenance, LANDED-node activations, unresolved-node HOLD/PARTIAL/STOP/non-load-bearing states, no orphan deformation nodes, honest termination, and Closure Witness / field_witness / Output Grapher agreement.

field_witness target role:

- Current: structural parser / reconstruction payload.
- Target: proof certificate over verified burden graph.
- Future invariant: `field_witness.collapse_complete = true` only if every diagnosed node has verified activation or explicit held/partial terminal state; otherwise `collapse_complete = false` and unresolved nodes are named.

Safe Shannon wording:

`The Shannon analogy is structurally useful because it clarifies why redundancy, canonicalization, and decoding checks matter. It does not by itself prove noetic collapse. It gives an engineering discipline: build encodings so drift becomes detectable inconsistency rather than plausible prose.`

Boltzmann Brain:

- Future stress case only, not current proof.
- Do not hardcode.

Implementation scope:

- Parses embedded parser-stable `field_witness` and requires non-empty `formal_reread_states[]`.
- Reuses existing `closure_witness_lib.py` and `check_mrp_generated_burden.py` normalization helpers.
- Requires formal state fields for source burden, prior Land, Delta, `R(H,Delta)`, route-gradient, divergence, curl, route result type, MRP resultant, graph delta, preemption basis, and route.
- Derives held route semantics: `held_burden_activation` must route to a `B_LA` burden, must not target generated `B_MRP`, must have graph edge coverage, and must carry an owner route.

Implementation:

- Defined canonical B.4 D0 normalization in `tools\check_graph_completeness.py`:
  - read raw input as UTF-8;
  - strip UTF-8 BOM if present;
  - normalize CRLF/CR to LF;
  - collapse whitespace runs to one space;
  - trim;
  - lowercase;
  - SHA-256 the resulting UTF-8 bytes.
- Added `--input` / `--input-path` to `tools\check_graph_completeness.py`.
- Certificate emission now:
  - computes `input_fingerprint` from raw D0 when `--input` is supplied;
  - requires supplied `--input-fingerprint` to match computed B.4 fingerprint;
  - requires any `field_witness.input_hash`, `input_fingerprint`, `input_sha256`, or
    provenance equivalent to match the computed B.4 fingerprint;
  - keeps `--input-fingerprint` as transitional compatibility when raw D0 is unavailable.
- Added raw D0 input fixtures.
- Added field-owned `provenance.input_hash` values to graph-completeness valid fixtures.

  - non-null/held/unresolved `∇×κ` must be accounted by LoopBreak, HOLD/PARTIAL/RECURSE,
    or non-load-bearing proof;
  - residual curl after LoopBreak must be held/partial/recurse or non-load-bearing rather
    than claimed resolved silently;
  - STOP/no-new-resultant remains legal only when divergence is neutral and curl is null/resolved
    or when explicit accounting exists.
- Added `divergence_curl_generated_burden_rules` to `tools\check_graph_completeness.py`.
- Added positive fixtures for generated divergence and LoopBreak-accounted curl.
- Added canaries for:
  - positive divergence with STOP/no resultant;
  - non-null curl with no LoopBreak/HOLD/PARTIAL/RECURSE;
  - LoopBreak that still leaves residual curl while claiming resolved closure;
  - generated positive-divergence target with no terminal/HOLD/PARTIAL accounting.

## B.2/B.4 Certificate Ownership Boundary Decision - 2026-05-30

Status: `PASS boundary clarified; PARTIAL broad retained-smoke sidecar adoption`.

Decision:

- Collapse certificates are checker-owned proof sidecars, not model-authored
  runtime/public output. `tools\check_graph_completeness.py --certificate`
  emits the B.2 certificate from the parsed governed output plus an explicit
  `--input` or `--input-fingerprint`.
- B.4 input binding is raw-D0/harness owned. `--input` computes the normalized
  input fingerprint; field-owned `input_hash` / `input_fingerprint` values are
  cross-checked when present but are not the source of proof.
- Certificate-backed Output Grapher proof mode remains a verifier: it consumes
  the sidecar certificate and raw input, recomputes B.1/B.2/B.4 agreement, and
  rejects graph-only or mismatched-certificate proof. Browser display remains
  advisory and does not replace the Python checker.

Evidence:

| Evidence | Source |
|---|---|
| Certificate emission requires proof-owned input | `tools\check_graph_completeness.py` exposes `--certificate`, `--input`, and `--input-fingerprint`, computes raw-input fingerprints, and errors without `--input`/`--input-fingerprint`. |
| Field-owned input hashes are cross-checks | `tools\check_graph_completeness.py` gathers field-owned input hashes and rejects mismatches against the raw-D0 fingerprint when `--input` is supplied. |
| Certificate sidecars validate independently | `schema\collapse-certificate.schema.json` and `tools\check_collapse_certificate_schema.py` validate B.2 certificate shape and invariants. |
| Grapher proof mode is verifier-owned | `tools\check_output_grapher.py --collapse-certificate --input` recomputes certificate agreement instead of treating graph reconstruction as proof. |
| Retained governed proofs already use sidecars | A9, source-order T_lang, restoration-track, C.7 LoopBreak, DAD8 C.8, and CD9A mixed-concealment sections above record raw input sidecars, certificate hashes, and certificate-backed Grapher checks. |

Boundary:

- Do not patch runtime guidance to ask the model to print inline collapse
  certificates by default.
- Do not treat model-authored proof booleans, inline certificate prose, browser
  graph rendering, or package availability as proof.
- The remaining B.2/B.4 work is harness/process adoption for retained smokes:
  raw input sidecar, checker-owned certificate sidecar, schema validation,
  certificate-backed Grapher check, and recorded hashes.
- A.13 hard register schema migration, D.8 subagent cleanup, and
  release/provenance remain frozen.

Next smallest safe action:

- Continue schema-light proof broadening or accepted-corpus consolidation using
  checker-owned B.1/B.2/B.4 sidecars. Do not open release/provenance from this
  boundary decision.

## B.1/B.2/B.4 Strict Proof-Sidecar Hash-Record Gate - 2026-05-31

Status: `PASS narrow harness/checker hardening; PARTIAL broad harness/default
adoption remains`.

Purpose: close the wrapper-sidecar false-pass and portability gap found during
post-v0.4.3.5 continuation. `tools/check_smoke_artifacts.py --hash-record`
validated `proof_sidecars` when present, but had no strict mode for lanes where
checker-owned sidecars were expected. The wrapper no-model self-test also wrote
its generated smoke hash JSON with `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`, which produces
a UTF-8 BOM under Windows PowerShell and caused the Python checker to reject the
record before the strict sidecar check could run.

  smoke hash record with no proof sidecars" from "proof-sidecar lane expected
  sidecars but omitted them."

- Updated `tools/run_current_skill_smoke.ps1` to write generated smoke hash JSON
  as UTF-8 without BOM and to run the checker in strict proof-sidecar mode
  during `-ProofSidecarSelfTest`.
- Updated `docs/audits/v0.4.3.0-retained-smoke-sidecar-convention.md` to record
  when strict sidecar validation is required and when sidecars remain optional.

## Live CI Hash-Portability Andon - 2026-05-31

Status: `PASS LIVE GITHUB CI AFTER HASH-PORTABILITY COUNTERMEASURE`.

Finding:

- The authorized push moved `main` from
  `81cd65e58e2b10b7582312630471f9e2e7227e60` to
  `040f39d744a3623d510f012fba0431b7de57c937`.
- GitHub Actions run `26711418685` failed in the single `runtime-checks`
  job, command block `Build and verify runtime`.
- First failing command: `python tools/check_hard_smoke_manifest.py`.

Failure evidence:

| Artifact | Expected | Found on GitHub Ubuntu checkout |
|---|---|---|
| `d1-rc4-seven-surface.input.txt` | `F3F717A8B2AA1793C6F6611C515380D7F5EA9FA1089AB5FF521266B5679B7EA2` | `05BB4B81E721BE1CF859115C774764E61CACB5626B802AA66B9C8B788B6875CC` |
| `d1-rc4-seven-surface-current-skill-87aa-run8.collapse_certificate.json` | `6356623AED013C15181A497A49D28951375C655FB56EE98A11C136B26F274F8B` | `0A84A03A72E648108344A3EF4242E92A05DE959E859BDA38AF8F69D5E6BC90DA` |
| `grapher/d1-rc4-seven-surface-current-skill-87aa-run8.html` | `1E88536AB5AAB886DC3E88AD399FA104DE5EAB08B10FCA80212092AD55346E78` | `CC89A8BA76838631FD99E4E6DC1376EFAB9C5ED3743933B284BAF9A3B37950E2` |

Root cause:

- `tools/check_hard_smoke_manifest.py` and
  `tools/check_retained_proof_corpus.py` hashed raw working-tree bytes.
- The tracked files have LF in the index but several local Windows working-tree
  copies were CRLF. Local Windows checks therefore accepted CRLF byte hashes,
  while GitHub's Ubuntu checkout computed LF byte hashes.
- This is a CI portability/manifest-contract issue, not a runtime behavior
  failure and not a release-gate/provenance issue.

Countermeasure:

- `tools/check_hard_smoke_manifest.py`: changed artifact hashing to
  repository-normalized text hashes (`CRLF`/bare `CR` normalized to `LF` for
  non-binary files), added an in-memory hash-portability self-test, and updated
  the raw-input error wording.
- `tools/check_retained_proof_corpus.py`: applied the same normalized text hash
  rule so the next CI command after hard-smoke cannot fail on the same
  line-ending class, and added the same in-memory hash-portability self-test.
- `tools/promote_retained_proof_case.py`: updated promotion-time hashes to
  produce the same normalized contract for future retained cases.
- Refreshed normalized hash fields in:
  - `tests/hard-smokes/v0.4.3.0-rc4-surfaces/valid/complete-manifest/hashes.json`;
  - `tests/hard-smokes/v0.4.3.0-rc4-surfaces/valid/d1-87aa-retained/d1-rc4-seven-surface-current-skill-87aa-run8.manifest-hashes.json`;
  - `tests/retained-proof-corpus/v0.4.3.0-schema-light/valid/sidecar-backed/manifest.json`.

Source-boundary fix:

- Commit: `2085a6a8b59fef1d738bec8a3a6baa70054820e7`
  (`v0.4.3.5: normalize proof-corpus manifest hashes`).
- Pushed range: `040f39d744a3623d510f012fba0431b7de57c937..2085a6a8b59fef1d738bec8a3a6baa70054820e7`.
- Replacement GitHub Actions run:
  `26711993147` (`https://github.com/theislampill/daee-epistemics/actions/runs/26711993147`).
- Live CI result: `success` on head SHA
  `2085a6a8b59fef1d738bec8a3a6baa70054820e7`.

## Retained Proof Corpus Promotion Helper - 2026-05-31

Status: `PASS helper/check-mode slice; no release/provenance`.

Purpose: reduce B.2/B.4 retained-sidecar drift by making governed-smoke
promotion repeatable. Before this slice, `check_retained_proof_corpus.py`
validated an already-written retained manifest, but copying sidecars and
constructing manifest entries remained manual. The new helper gives future
lanes a deterministic promotion/check path without changing runtime behavior.

Files changed:

- `tools/promote_retained_proof_case.py`
- `docs/audits/v0.4.3.0-retained-smoke-sidecar-convention.md`
- `docs/audits/v0.4.3.0-open-work-ledger.md`
- `docs/audits/v0.4.3.0-implementaudit-orchestrator.md`

- validates source raw input, governed output, checker-owned collapse
  certificate, and warning-clean certificate-backed Grapher HTML;
- checks the collapse certificate schema and verifies its input fingerprint
  against the raw input sidecar;
- computes retained artifact hashes and builds the manifest entry;
- in `--check` mode, compares a proposed promotion against the existing
  retained case and manifest without writing;
- in write mode, copies the four canonical retained artifacts and appends or
  replaces the manifest entry only when explicitly invoked.
